task.description: WF-02 Step 1b (Design gate) for REQ-037. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-037.md independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary), re-derived every checkable claim against the live source files, and checked all 10 acceptance criteria per GitHub issue #69 for a corresponding, fully-specified, non-deferred design element.
acceptance_criteria: AC1-AC10 per GitHub issue #69 / docs/agents/requirements.yaml REQ-037 (full text read via gh issue view 69)

result.summary:
PASS. Independently re-read docs/agents/design/REQ-037.md in full (not the designer's summary) and verified every load-bearing claim against live source:

1. Schema/zero-schema-change (design §0): confirmed apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts:333-370 invite_codes has id, eventId, code (unique), issuedToUserId (nullable FK->users.id), grantsCompanionOf (nullable FK->users.id), maxUses (not null), usedCount (not null default 0), expiresAt (nullable), createdAt, updatedAt -- every field the design uses genuinely exists, none invented. registrations schema confirms inviteCodeId (line 281, FK->inviteCodes.id) and invitedByUserId (line 272) both pre-existing. generateInviteCode() in apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts confirmed exported and used unchanged (no redefinition proposed). DATA-DESIGNER-not-needed conclusion re-derived independently: no new entity/relationship/migration is implied anywhere in the design; it composes only pre-existing columns. Correct.

2. Three-command shape (design §1): grepped organizerRequests.ts and schema.ts comments -- codebase convention is confirmed one-verb-per-command (venue_new/event_new/staff_add pattern referenced matches actual naming visible in organizerRequests.ts's req:open:<id> callback convention and requireOrganizerForChapter call sites). The three shapes' differing required arguments (target user vs. use count vs. host user) genuinely justify three parse functions over one branching command; this is not an invented pattern, it matches REQ-033's own already-adopted no-type-enum precedent restated at the command layer.

3. Refusal order (design §2): traced against the actual apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts -- isFinished(endsAt, evaluationTime) confirmed at event.ts:755-757, taking evaluationTime as an explicit caller-supplied parameter (matches decisions/0006, no new predicate, no internal new Date()). getEventById (event.ts:519+) confirmed to already select status and endsAt in its returned row -- no new query needed for the cancelled/finished checks. Order (event resolve -> auth -> cancelled -> finished) matches organizerRequests.ts's actual call-site ordering (requireOrganizerForChapter invoked immediately after getEventById, before any business-rule check, at every one of its ~8 call sites grepped).

4. Bot-never-sends reasoning (design §5): stated as a genuine platform-fact argument (Telegram's Bot API cannot open a conversation to a chat_id that has never started the bot), not merely asserted -- and internally consistent with AC3's requirement that a PERSONAL code work for a tg_id=NULL user: since that user has structurally never started the bot, no delivery channel can exist at issue time regardless of any hypothetical send-policy choice. git grep over apps/bot for sendMessage/ctx.reply/bot.api patterns near 'invite' returned nothing (the design artefact does not yet exist as code, consistent with Step 1 being design-only) -- the design's own git-grep-verifiable-negative claim (AC9) is a correct forward-looking specification, not a runtime check misplaced at this gate.

5. S3-safe redeemer query (design §4.2): the specified SELECT structurally omits profiles.phone and profiles.email from its select-clause column list (registrationId, firstName, lastName, tgUsername, company only) -- matches the exact structural-exclusion pattern already used by listPendingRequestsForOrganizer (registration.ts:1597-1624, confirmed by direct read: its own select clause also omits phone/email). This satisfies S3 by construction, not by a runtime filter.

6. AC7 read-only claim (design §4.1-4.2): both specified queries are plain SELECTs; no UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE against invite_codes appears anywhere in the read path the design specifies. Confirmed no write statement is present in either query block.

7. AC5 (codes work on any event, not gated on requires_invite): design §2 step 5 explicitly states this is NOT a check ('Nothing in this design reads requiresInvite or requiresApproval at issuing time') -- an explicit non-check statement, not a silent omission, satisfying the handoff's specific instruction on this point.

8. Acceptance-criteria coverage: all 10 ACs from GitHub issue #69 map to a concrete, non-deferred design element (design §9's table cross-checked against the issue's own AC list) -- no 'TBD'/'TODO'/deferral language found anywhere in the artefact.

9. Props/types: IssueInviteCodeInput/IssueInviteCodeValidation (§1.5), InviteCodeListItem/InviteCodeRedeemer/InviteCodeDetail (§4.1/§4.2) are all fully field-level specified with concrete TypeScript shapes -- no vague placeholder types.

10. No implementation code: the entire artefact contains only type/interface declarations, SQL-shaped query descriptions (not actual drizzle query builder code), a lookup table (§4.3), and prose -- no function body, no actual .ts control flow. Consistent with REQ-033/035/036 precedent artefacts.

11. Design-system tokens: N/A correctly and explicitly stated (§8) -- this is a Telegram bot conversation surface with no apps/web rendering, so tokens.css has no applicable entries to check; this is consistent with the repo's own site/bot surface split (WF-02 Step 0.9) and matches REQ-033/035/036's own artefacts taking the same N/A stance.

All checks pass. No rework required.
